facts.text: Leverage has fallen because reported EBITDA grew while carrying-value debt stayed close to flat. Pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-07-28, net debt to reported EBITDA is negative 0.09x. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C29; calculation C30; calculation C59

Cash paid for interest is printed net of interest received and the gross amount is not stated, so the interest cover on cash interest paid is not a stress measure; severity Medium; the issuer's interest paid and interest income detail would close it, and the cover on the note coupon is shown beside it.
The yearly maturity schedule is printed only at 2025-09-30, so the maturity wall at 2026-06-30 is drawn from that date; severity Low; the fiscal 2026 annual report would close it.
Finance leases of USD 4.9 million have no stated security or rank and are left out of the debt stack; severity Low; the lease agreements or an issuer statement of rank would close it.

The filings print dashes that are carried as gaps: in the income statement Goodwill impairment (FY2023, FY2025); Pension (benefit) expense other than service (Q3 2025, Q2 2026, H1 2026); Other expense (FY2023, FY2025); in the cash flow statement Goodwill impairment (FY2023, FY2025); Non-cash asset impairment (FY2023, H1 2026); (Gain) loss on sale of assets (Q1 2025); Proceeds from sales of assets (Q1 2025); Stock repurchased under buyback program (Q1 2025); Debt issuance costs (FY2023, FY2025); severity Low; the issuer's statement that a dash means nil would close it.

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a Low rating is that nothing in the supplied documents shows a structural barrier to a debt-funded transaction. No controlling holder is named, the direction of the unnamed transaction is not stated, and cash of USD 495.3 million plus USD 163.7 million of ABL availability could fund a deal without a new issue. The change-of-control put needs a ratings decline, and the indenture and credit agreement that set the baskets for payments, investments and added debt are not supplied, so what the documents permit is not established and the rating rests on documented behaviour. Customer concentration is the largest business risk, with two customers at 37% of gross sales. The view would worsen if the transaction proves debt funded or large against earnings, if a holder emerges with a stake that changes control, if payouts exceed free cash flow, or if a second waiver is needed. It would improve if the transaction is a small cash-funded disposal or bolt-on and the proxy statement shows dispersed ownership. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Earnings have recovered on price rather than volume, so the gain is less durable than the margin suggests. Reported EBITDA rose 81.10% from USD 186.2 million in FY2023 to USD 337.2 million for the twelve months to 2026-06-30 on net sales growth of 15.96%, an incremental margin of 74.17%, and the 4.73% growth of nine months 2026 came from higher pricing with slightly lower volumes. The same operating leverage works in reverse: a return to FY2022 net sales would remove EBITDA at 69.51% of the lost sales. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M14; calculation M15; calculation M17; calculation M10

No sponsor or controlling holder is named, dividends and repurchases took 43.67% of free cash flow in nine months 2026, and lender treatment has been orderly, but an unnamed transaction and the unsupplied debt documents leave event risk and legal capacity open. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against the strong view is that the earnings base is price-led and partly non-recurring: an incremental margin of 74.17% on 15.96% sales growth, unquantified third-quarter tariff refunds, guidance that implies a softer fourth quarter, and free cash flow at 59.14% of adjusted net income against guidance of above 70%. Concentration compounds it, since two customers at 37% of gross sales can reprice or leave together. The view survives because it rests on the balance sheet rather than margins: at FY2022 earnings total debt is still only 2.57x and liquidity stays USD 128.0 million above the notes. It would weaken if fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA lands below USD 90.3 million, if free cash flow stays below 70% of adjusted net income, if the unnamed transaction is debt funded, or if either large customer is lost. It would strengthen if the fourth quarter holds the third-quarter margin without refunds and cash is applied to the notes. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M14; calculation M15; calculation M29; calculation M25; calculation M19; calculation M22; calculation M9

facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Mueller Water makes the valves, hydrants, pipe repair products, gas products, metering systems and leak detection products that water utilities use to move and measure water in the United States and Canada, with FY2025 net sales of USD 1,429.7 million split 57.70% Water Flow Solutions and 42.30% Water Management Solutions. Municipal repair and replacement drives 60% to 65% of sales and utilities specify the products from a large installed base, so cash flow has more visibility than most industrial manufacturers; but 91.89% of sales are in the United States and two customers hold 37% of gross sales, so that visibility rests on one country and a few channel relationships. The seasonal pattern leaves the first half weakest, which is why the undrawn facility matters for liquidity preservation. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation M10; calculation M9

facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: No sponsor or controlling holder is named, so no owner can extract value or step in with support, and policy is set by the board: dividends and repurchases took 43.67% of free cash flow in nine months 2026 and none was debt funded. Substantially all U.S. subsidiaries borrow under the facility and guarantee the notes, which rank behind secured facility borrowings on U.S. inventory and receivables, and the put at 101% on a change of control applies only with a ratings decline whose definition is not supplied, so takeover protection for noteholders is thin; legal capacity for distributions and added debt is not established. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is predictable in its municipal core and cyclical at the edges. Water and sewerage rates rose 4.6% in the twelve months to 2025-09-30, which supports replacement budgets, while total housing starts fell 1.1% in FY2025 with single-family starts down 5.2%, and management expects a slowdown in new residential construction. Nine-month 2026 net sales grew 4.73% on pricing with slightly lower volumes, so pricing power is demonstrated but volume growth is not, and the backlog of USD 320.7 million, 6.02% above a year earlier, gives some visibility; pass-through works through price actions that the issuer says only mostly offset tariff costs. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 56; EX-99.1_2026-05-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation M11; calculation M10

facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: A significant portion of costs is fixed, so margins depend on volume and price. Purchased parts are about 35% and raw materials about 8% of cost of sales, tariffs add about 3% of cost of sales and inflation about 4%, and 42% of the United States workforce is under agreements expiring between December 2025 and October 2027. The EBITDA margin rose from 14.60% to 22.79% with a 74.17% incremental margin, and falling back to FY2022 sales would remove EBITDA at 69.51% of the lost sales, so margins can be defended only while pricing holds and volume does not fall far. facts.label: Capital intensity and free cash flow conversion
facts.text: Capital intensity is moderate but rising and conversion of earnings into free cash flow is falling. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Mueller Water presents a strong business and financial profile supported by low leverage, USD 659.0 million of liquidity and entrenched municipal demand, but credit quality is constrained by price-led margins, two customers at 37% of gross sales and weakening cash conversion. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because municipal replacement anchors demand while earnings and cash conversion rest on pricing. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on whether cash is kept against the notes, which it covers 1.10x, and on extending the facility before 2029-03-16. The primary downside path is a price-led margin reversal with a customer loss and an inventory-driven cash drain, which at FY2022 earnings would leave total debt at 2.57x. Against typical leveraged credit issuers the financial profile looks stronger than the business profile, but that comparison is qualitative because no peer set is supplied. Further analysis would require the fiscal fourth quarter, customer terms, the executed debt documents and peer data. Fundamental credit completed with limitations. Top risk: reversal of price-led margins with two customers at 37% of sales. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M4; calculation M9; calculation M23; calculation M19

## Findings
### Bottom line

The eight supplied filings and releases support a credit snapshot of Mueller Water as of the quarter ended 2026-06-30, with limitations: creditors can rely on the June 2026 balance sheet, but nothing after 2026-08-06 is supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, page 1

Both annual reports, all three fiscal 2026 quarterly reports and their releases are present, so the balance sheet, with USD 495.3 million of cash and USD 659.0 million of total liquidity, the debt terms, the ratings and the segment results are sourced. ## Findings
### Bottom line

Mueller Water is in a net cash position at 2026-06-30, with USD 495.3 million of cash against USD 452.9 million of carrying-value debt, so creditors face low leverage and no material maturity until June 2029.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C5

On reported EBITDA of USD 337.2 million for the twelve months to that date, total debt is 1.34x and net debt is negative 0.13x; net debt is negative USD 42.4 million, or negative USD 31.5 million pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-07-28. The issuer states only adjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is calculated here, and cash interest paid is net of interest received.
Basis: calculation C29; calculation C5; calculation C39; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, page 5
### Key findings

Leverage has fallen because reported EBITDA grew while carrying-value debt stayed close to flat. Debt was USD 449.5 million at 2024-09-30 and USD 452.9 million at 2026-06-30, while reported EBITDA rose from USD 242.3 million in FY2024 to USD 307.7 million in FY2025 and USD 337.2 million for the twelve months to 2026-06-30. Total debt to reported EBITDA therefore fell from 1.86x to 1.47x and then 1.34x, and net debt to reported EBITDA fell from 0.58x to 0.07x and then negative 0.13x, as cash rose from USD 309.9 million to USD 431.5 million and then USD 495.3 million. On adjusted EBITDA of USD 368.5 million, built from the issuer's quarterly figures, the latest ratios are 1.23x and negative 0.12x, so reported EBITDA is the more conservative base. Pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-07-28, net debt to reported EBITDA is negative 0.09x.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C29; calculation C30; calculation C59

The capital structure is one USD 450.0 million 4.0% senior unsecured note due June 2029, guaranteed by substantially all U.S. subsidiaries and subordinate to an undrawn USD 175.0 million asset-based facility, plus small finance leases. Because 99.21% of scheduled principal falls in fiscal 2029, refinancing risk sits on one date, and the asset-based facility matures on 2029-03-16 while the notes remain outstanding, about three months earlier, so the liquidity backstop ends before the notes do. A refinancing therefore needs to be addressed before the facility expires, not only when the notes fall due.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 114–115; calculation C37; calculation C55

Cash interest paid is net of interest received, at USD 3.9 million for the twelve months to 2026-06-30, so the reported cover of 86.46x overstates protection. The notes carry USD 18.0 million of annual cash coupon, which reported EBITDA of USD 337.2 million covers 18.73x, the more useful measure of fixed-charge cover.
Basis: calculation C31; calculation C58; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 36

Free cash flow, defined as operating cash flow less capital expenditures, was USD 172.0 million in FY2025 and USD 110.6 million in nine months 2026, but conversion of reported EBITDA fell to 43.42% from 45.74% a year earlier, because inventories absorbed USD 59.9 million and capital expenditures rose to USD 43.6 million from USD 32.8 million, mainly for iron foundries. Dividends and repurchases of USD 48.3 million in nine months 2026 were covered more than twice by free cash flow.
Basis: calculation C44; calculation C50; calculation C45; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 35

Liquidity was USD 659.0 million at 2026-06-30: cash of USD 495.3 million plus USD 163.7 million of availability under the asset-based facility, which is net of USD 11.1 million of letters of credit. Of the cash, USD 116.6 million, or 23.54%, is held in Israel, Canada and China, where earnings are treated as permanently reinvested, so only part of the cash is readily available to the U.S. borrowers of the notes and the facility.
Basis: calculation C36; calculation C53; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 60

Outside the debt figure sit operating lease liabilities of USD 28.4 million at 2025-09-30, letters of credit of USD 11.1 million, surety bonds of USD 13.2 million and a New Markets Tax Credit investor contribution of USD 4.8 million carried in other liabilities; the defined benefit pension plan, by contrast, is overfunded by USD 19.5 million at that date and is an asset. The environmental indemnity on the former U.S. Pipe site carries no accrual because its cost cannot be estimated, which leaves an unquantified claim outside debt.
Basis: calculation C57; calculation C56; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10

Two definition choices matter when comparing figures. The 2026-08-05 release quotes total debt of USD 452.9 million at carrying value while the debt note prints USD 454.9 million gross, a difference of USD 2.0 million of deferred financing costs, and the issuer's adjusted EBITDA adds back USD 22.0 million of nine-month charges that reported EBITDA keeps, so adjusted EBITDA runs higher than reported EBITDA by that amount in nine months 2026.
Basis: calculation C40; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, page 5

The only post-balance-sheet event the documents state is a quarterly dividend declared on 2026-07-28 with an estimated cash outlay of USD 10.9 million, which moves net debt from negative USD 42.4 million to negative USD 31.5 million and net leverage from negative 0.13x to negative 0.09x; it is kept out of period figures.
Basis: calculation C39; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 36
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The net cash position is thinner than it looks: counting only cash held outside Israel, Canada and China, net debt is USD 74.2 million, or 0.22x reported EBITDA, because USD 116.6 million of the cash is held abroad. Free cash flow conversion also fell to 43.42% in nine months 2026 from 78.99% in FY2024. The view would weaken if the unnamed transaction behind the transaction-related expenses were funded with debt, if distributions rose above free cash flow, or if conversion kept falling while capital expenditures stayed near USD 43.6 million for nine months.
Basis: calculation C54; calculation C50; calculation C53
### Limitations

Reported EBITDA is calculated here because the issuer states only adjusted EBITDA, and the adjusted amount for FY2025 and every twelve-month figure are built from issuer-stated quarters rather than printed.
Basis: calculation C19; calculation C29
Cash interest paid is stated net of interest received and the gross amount is not stated, so no ratio on actual gross interest paid can be formed.

The interim statements are unaudited, the filings print dashes that are carried as gaps rather than zero, and the maturity schedule is dated 2025-09-30 because the later filings print no yearly maturities.

## Gaps
Each gap lists what is missing, what it restricts, its severity and the action that would close it.

The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA in any supplied document, so EBITDA (Reported) is calculated for every period and every leverage and cover ratio rests on a calculated base; severity Medium; the definition is disclosed in the income statement table and only the issuer can state its own figure.

Adjusted EBITDA is not supplied for FY2023 and FY2024, so the adjusted ratios for fiscal 2024 and the fiscal 2024 adjusted chart point are not calculable; severity Medium; adding the fourth-quarter releases for fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2025 would close it.

The full-year and fourth-quarter FY2025 adjusted EBITDA are not printed in any supplied document and are built from the first-quarter FY2026 release, which restricts every twelve-month adjusted figure to that derivation; severity Low; the fourth-quarter FY2025 release would close it.

Cash paid for interest is printed net of interest received and the gross amount is not stated, so the interest cover on cash interest paid is not a stress measure; severity Medium; the issuer's interest paid and interest income detail would close it, and the cover on the note coupon is shown beside it.
The yearly maturity schedule is printed only at 2025-09-30, so the maturity wall at 2026-06-30 is drawn from that date; severity Low; the fiscal 2026 annual report would close it.
Finance leases of USD 4.9 million have no stated security or rank and are left out of the debt stack; severity Low; the lease agreements or an issuer statement of rank would close it.

The filings print dashes that are carried as gaps: in the income statement Goodwill impairment (FY2023, FY2025); Pension (benefit) expense other than service (Q3 2025, Q2 2026, H1 2026); Other expense (FY2023, FY2025); in the cash flow statement Goodwill impairment (FY2023, FY2025); Non-cash asset impairment (FY2023, H1 2026); (Gain) loss on sale of assets (Q1 2025); Proceeds from sales of assets (Q1 2025); Stock repurchased under buyback program (Q1 2025); Debt issuance costs (FY2023, FY2025); severity Low; the issuer's statement that a dash means nil would close it.

Some lines are not printed in every interim statement: goodwill impairment and other expense appear only in the annual income statement, the pension line is absent from the first-quarter columns, and discrete second-quarter and third-quarter cash flows are not printed because the quarterly reports show year-to-date cash flows only; severity Low; no further document is needed because the year-to-date columns are given.

The balance sheet at 2025-06-30 is not in the supplied filings, so a third-quarter 2025 net debt and the twelve-month ratios at that date are not stated; severity Low; the third-quarter fiscal 2025 report would close it.

The transaction behind the transaction-related expenses is not named in any supplied document, so any effect on debt or cash from it is not established; severity Medium; a later filing or release naming the transaction would close it.
The nine months 2024 column is not in the supplied filings, so net sales growth for nine months 2025 is not stated; severity Low; the third-quarter fiscal 2025 report would close it.
Backlog is stated only at fiscal year end, so backlog at the interim dates is not stated; severity Low; no document in the supply states it and the issuer's annual report is the only source.

The carrying value of the notes and of the finance leases separately, the security, rank, coupon and yearly principal of the finance leases, and any floor on the ABL rate are not stated in the supplied documents; severity Low; the credit agreement and the lease schedule would close them.

The per-share, share-count and dividend-per-share lines of the income statement and the comprehensive income and equity statements are not extracted because they do not enter a credit metric; severity Low; no action is needed for the credit work.

Nothing after 2026-08-06 is supplied, so any financing, repayment or rating event after the declared dividend is not established; severity Medium; the fourth-quarter release and any current reports to the cutoff would close it.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Mueller Water names no sponsor or controlling shareholder in the supplied filings, and its financial policy returns modest cash to shareholders without debt funding, so governance adds little creditor risk beyond a concentrated distributor base.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation K21

Sponsor and governance risk is Low. Dividends and buybacks took 43.67% of free cash flow in nine months 2026, the only waiver the documents record lasted 57 days after a cyber incident, and the cash flow statements show no acquisition spending from FY2023 to nine months 2026. The unnamed transaction behind up to USD 22.0 million of nine-month charges and the unsupplied proxy statement are the open points.
Basis: 10-K_2024-09-30_mwa-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; calculation K21; calculation K41; calculation K34
### Key findings

Ownership gives creditors no sponsor to extract value, but also no controlling holder to defend the company against a change of control. The filings name no sponsor or large holder, list 78 holders of record, and leave beneficial ownership to a proxy statement that is not supplied. The notes carry a put at 101% on a change of control only when a ratings decline accompanies it, and the indenture's definition of that decline is not supplied, so a takeover without it would leave noteholders with no put. The notes were rated Ba1 and BB+ at 2026-06-30.

Shareholder returns are modest and covered by free cash flow today, but in the weakest year they exceeded it. Dividends and repurchases were USD 48.3 million in nine months 2026, 43.67% of free cash flow of USD 110.6 million, against 33.08% in FY2025 and 26.07% in FY2024, and the quarterly dividend per share rose 4.48%. In FY2023 the outlay took 78.34% of free cash flow of USD 61.4 million, and in FY2022 free cash flow was negative USD 2.4 million against USD 71.5 million returned, met from cash; the next year only repurchases were cut, from USD 35.0 million to USD 10.0 million. No borrowing appears in the financing sections from FY2022 to nine months 2026, and USD 49.5 million of the USD 250.0 million repurchase authorization remains.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2024-09-30_mwa-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 94; calculation K21; calculation K20; calculation K19; calculation K18; calculation K14; calculation K12; calculation K13; calculation K17; calculation K35

Financial policy keeps debt flat while cash builds, which protects liquidity but commits to no deleveraging. Debt was USD 452.9 million and cash USD 495.3 million at 2026-06-30, against cash of USD 160.3 million at the end of FY2023. The notes have been redeemable at specified prices since 2024-06-15 and their principal is unchanged at USD 450.0 million; the issuer says only that liquidity may fund voluntary debt prepayments and repurchases based on excess cash flows, and that it may consider prepayment, refinancing or new debt.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32

An unnamed transaction is the main open governance question. Up to USD 22.0 million of nine-month 2026 charges may relate to it, yet no document names the counterparty, direction, price or funding. The cash flow statements show no acquisition spending from FY2023 to nine months 2026, so there is no integration record to read, and management said in May 2026 that the balance sheet gives ample capacity for acquisitions. With cash above debt a cash-funded deal would leave leverage low, but a debt-funded one would not.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; EX-99.1_2026-05-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 94; calculation K34

Lender treatment has been orderly. The December 2023 waiver capped ABL borrowings at USD 50.0 million until delayed reports were delivered after the October 2023 cyber incident and ended after 57 days; the amendment of 2024-03-28 then extended the facility from 2025-07-29 to 2029 and cut margins by about 50 bp. No exchange, priming or non-pro-rata transaction is stated in any supplied document. The facility now matures 91 days before the notes, so the liquidity line ends first.
Basis: 10-K_2024-09-30_mwa-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 116; calculation K41; calculation K39

Leadership has changed at the top within 343 days, but the chief executive succession is internal, which limits policy discontinuity. The chief financial officer started on 2025-03-03, the chief accounting officer on 2025-08-15 and the new chief executive on 2026-02-09, having been president and chief operating officer since May 2024; the chair is non-executive. Transition costs sit inside the strategic reorganization charges of USD 18.9 million for nine months 2026.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-Q_2026-03-31_mwa-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation K40

Revenue is anchored by municipal repair demand but concentrated in two customers. They bought 37% of FY2025 gross sales and owed 46.67% of net receivables at 2025-09-30, and the business section puts the two largest distributors at the same combined 37%. Municipal repair and replacement drove 60% to 65% of FY2025 net sales on management's estimate, the installed base and utility specification support repeat demand, and backlog of USD 320.7 million was 6.02% above a year earlier. Yet the distributors hold no long-term contracts and also carry competing products, so a loss or repricing would hit sales, margin and collections together.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 127; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation K10; calculation K29

Margins sit at a high that is partly non-recurring, so the earnings base behind payouts is less secure than the trend suggests. Gross margin rose from 29.75% in FY2023 to 36.14% in FY2025 and 38.24% in nine months 2026, and the Water Flow Solutions operating margin from 12.55% to 29.77%, on manufacturing efficiency, volume and pricing in FY2024 and on pricing and the closure of the legacy brass foundry in nine months 2026; the third quarter also included tariff refunds the issuer calls non-recurring and does not quantify. Inflation of about 4% and tariffs of about 3% of cost of sales continue, and capital expenditure guidance for FY2026 is 26.85% to 37.42% above FY2025.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2024-09-30_mwa-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation K22; calculation K24; calculation K26; calculation K27; calculation K32
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a Low rating is that nothing in the supplied documents shows a structural barrier to a debt-funded transaction. No controlling holder is named, the direction of the unnamed transaction is not stated, and cash of USD 495.3 million plus USD 163.7 million of ABL availability could fund a deal without a new issue. The change-of-control put needs a ratings decline, and the indenture and credit agreement that set the baskets for payments, investments and added debt are not supplied, so what the documents permit is not established and the rating rests on documented behaviour. Customer concentration is the largest business risk, with two customers at 37% of gross sales. The view would worsen if the transaction proves debt funded or large against earnings, if a holder emerges with a stake that changes control, if payouts exceed free cash flow, or if a second waiver is needed. It would improve if the transaction is a small cash-funded disposal or bolt-on and the proxy statement shows dispersed ownership.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 127; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation K34
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so beneficial ownership, board independence, related-party dealings and fees are not established; the finding of no controlling holder rests on the filings' silence and would reverse if a large holder exists.

- The transaction-related charges name no counterparty, direction, price or funding, so the transaction summary lists no terms and the low acquisition-risk reading cannot be extended to the deal itself.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9

- Only the issuer's summaries of the indenture and ABL are supplied, so legal capacity for distributions, investments and added debt is not established; the Low risk level rests on documented behaviour, not on what the documents permit.
- The tariff refunds that lifted third-quarter margins are not quantified, so the durability of the margin gain, and with it the coverage of payouts by free cash flow, cannot be tested without them.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 27–29

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No acquisition, merger, divestiture, buyout or recapitalisation is described in any supplied document, and the cash flow statements show no acquisition spending from FY2023 to nine months 2026. The USD 450.0 million 4.0% senior notes due 2029-06-15 were issued on 2021-05-28 and, with cash on hand, redeemed the previous notes; they remain the only bond, are guaranteed by substantially all U.S. subsidiaries and rank behind borrowings under the USD 175.0 million asset-based facility, which was not drawn during the quarter ended 2026-06-30.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, page 5

The only transaction signal is an expense line. Portfolio optimization costs of USD 3.1 million in cost of sales and strategic reorganization charges of USD 18.9 million for nine months 2026 are described as including transaction-related expenses, leadership transition costs, an impairment and severance. No counterparty, nature, price, timing or funding is stated, so the transaction is not established, and up to USD 22.0 million of nine-month costs may relate to it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation K34

Two lender-side steps frame the creditor position. The December 2023 waiver capped ABL borrowings at USD 50.0 million until delayed reports were delivered and ended on 2024-02-06, and the amendment of 2024-03-28 extended the facility's maturity from 2025-07-29 to the earlier of 2029-03-28 and 91 days before the notes mature, and cut margins by about 50 bp.
Basis: 10-K_2024-09-30_mwa-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 116; calculation K41

A New Markets Tax Credit financing entered into on 2020-12-22 funded part of the Decatur foundry. The issuer expects the investor to exercise a put in December 2027 for nominal consideration, which would leave the issuer sole owner and give an estimated gain of USD 3.9 million, and it indemnifies the investor against recapture of the tax credits.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10

## Findings
### Bottom line

Mueller Water's fundamental credit profile is strong: total debt is 1.34x reported EBITDA and liquidity is 1.46x the notes, so creditors face little near-term default risk, while price-led margins, two customers at 37% of sales and one 2029 maturity are the constraints.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M2; calculation M23

Reported EBITDA was USD 337.2 million for the twelve months to 2026-06-30, net debt is negative USD 42.4 million (negative USD 31.5 million pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-07-28) and liquidity is USD 659.0 million against USD 450.0 million of notes due 2029-06-15. A return to FY2022 earnings would lift total debt to 2.57x without threatening liquidity.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M1; calculation M3; calculation M4; calculation M19
### Key findings

Leverage and liquidity are the strongest support. Total debt is 1.34x reported EBITDA and net debt to reported EBITDA is negative 0.13x, or negative 0.09x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-07-28, while liquidity of USD 659.0 million is 1.46x the notes and the notes were quoted at 96.91% of principal at 2026-06-30. Because the facility is undrawn and the only bond falls due in June 2029, creditors face no scheduled call on liquidity until then.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation M2; calculation M3; calculation M23; calculation M24

Earnings have recovered on price rather than volume, so the gain is less durable than the margin suggests. Reported EBITDA rose 81.10% from USD 186.2 million in FY2023 to USD 337.2 million for the twelve months to 2026-06-30 on net sales growth of 15.96%, an incremental margin of 74.17%, and the 4.73% growth of nine months 2026 came from higher pricing with slightly lower volumes. The same operating leverage works in reverse: a return to FY2022 net sales would remove EBITDA at 69.51% of the lost sales.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M14; calculation M15; calculation M17; calculation M10

Guidance points to a softer fourth quarter, which tests how much of the third-quarter strength repeats. Fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of USD 367 million to USD 372 million implies USD 90.3 million to USD 95.3 million for the fourth quarter, 15.92% to 11.27% below the third quarter, although the fourth quarter of FY2025 was 6.25% above its third, and implied fourth-quarter net sales are 2.44% below to 0.18% above a year earlier. The third quarter included tariff refunds that the issuer calls non-recurring and does not quantify.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation M25; calculation M26; calculation M28; calculation M27

Demand is anchored in municipal replacement but concentrated in two customers, which is the main business risk. Municipal repair and replacement was 60% to 65% of FY2025 net sales on management's estimate and backlog was 6.02% higher at year-end, yet two customers bought 37% of FY2025 gross sales and owed 46.67% of net receivables, with no long-term contracts and competing products on their shelves, so a loss or repricing would hit sales, margin and collections together.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 127; calculation M9; calculation M10

Cash conversion is weakening, which limits how much of the earnings gain reaches creditors. Free cash flow was 43.42% of reported EBITDA in nine months 2026 against 78.99% in FY2024, because inventories absorbed USD 59.9 million and capital expenditures rose 32.93%, and it was 59.14% of adjusted net income against guidance of above 70%, which the issuer cut from above 85%.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against the strong view is that the earnings base is price-led and partly non-recurring: an incremental margin of 74.17% on 15.96% sales growth, unquantified third-quarter tariff refunds, guidance that implies a softer fourth quarter, and free cash flow at 59.14% of adjusted net income against guidance of above 70%. Concentration compounds it, since two customers at 37% of gross sales can reprice or leave together. The view survives because it rests on the balance sheet rather than margins: at FY2022 earnings total debt is still only 2.57x and liquidity stays USD 128.0 million above the notes. It would weaken if fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA lands below USD 90.3 million, if free cash flow stays below 70% of adjusted net income, if the unnamed transaction is debt funded, or if either large customer is lost. It would strengthen if the fourth quarter holds the third-quarter margin without refunds and cash is applied to the notes.

### Company description

Mueller Water makes the valves, hydrants, pipe repair products, gas products, metering systems and leak detection products that water utilities use to move and measure water in the United States and Canada, with FY2025 net sales of USD 1,429.7 million split 57.70% Water Flow Solutions and 42.30% Water Management Solutions. Municipal repair and replacement drives 60% to 65% of sales and utilities specify the products from a large installed base, so cash flow has more visibility than most industrial manufacturers; but 91.89% of sales are in the United States and two customers hold 37% of gross sales, so that visibility rests on one country and a few channel relationships. The seasonal pattern leaves the first half weakest, which is why the undrawn facility matters for liquidity preservation.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation M10; calculation M9
### Ownership and group structure

No sponsor or controlling holder is named, so no owner can extract value or step in with support, and policy is set by the board: dividends and repurchases took 43.67% of free cash flow in nine months 2026 and none was debt funded. Substantially all U.S. subsidiaries borrow under the facility and guarantee the notes, which rank behind secured facility borrowings on U.S. inventory and receivables, and the put at 101% on a change of control applies only with a ratings decline whose definition is not supplied, so takeover protection for noteholders is thin; legal capacity for distributions and added debt is not established.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; calculation M9
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is predictable in its municipal core and cyclical at the edges. Water and sewerage rates rose 4.6% in the twelve months to 2025-09-30, which supports replacement budgets, while total housing starts fell 1.1% in FY2025 with single-family starts down 5.2%, and management expects a slowdown in new residential construction. Nine-month 2026 net sales grew 4.73% on pricing with slightly lower volumes, so pricing power is demonstrated but volume growth is not, and the backlog of USD 320.7 million, 6.02% above a year earlier, gives some visibility; pass-through works through price actions that the issuer says only mostly offset tariff costs.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 56; EX-99.1_2026-05-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation M11; calculation M10
### Cost structure and margin resilience

A significant portion of costs is fixed, so margins depend on volume and price. Purchased parts are about 35% and raw materials about 8% of cost of sales, tariffs add about 3% of cost of sales and inflation about 4%, and 42% of the United States workforce is under agreements expiring between December 2025 and October 2027. The EBITDA margin rose from 14.60% to 22.79% with a 74.17% incremental margin, and falling back to FY2022 sales would remove EBITDA at 69.51% of the lost sales, so margins can be defended only while pricing holds and volume does not fall far.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation M12; calculation M16; calculation M14; calculation M17
### Capital intensity and free cash flow conversion

Capital intensity is moderate but rising and conversion of earnings into free cash flow is falling. Capital expenditures were up 32.93% in nine months 2026, are guided to USD 60 million to USD 65 million for FY2026 and were 17.23% of reported EBITDA for the latest twelve months, while free cash flow conversion fell from 78.99% in FY2024 to 55.90% in FY2025 and 43.42% in nine months 2026 as inventories absorbed USD 59.9 million. The filings do not split maintenance from growth spending, so flexibility to cut capital expenditures ahead of the 2029 maturity cannot be measured.

### Porter's five forces

Rivalry is moderate. The issuer says there are only a few competitors for most products and that end users are slow to change brands, which protects pricing, but most competitors are not publicly traded, so their behaviour cannot be monitored; the creditor implication is limited price-war risk with little visibility on it.

The threat of new entrants is low. Products must meet water works standards and be specified by utilities, and municipalities approve a limited number of hydrant brands, so entry is slow and margins are better protected than in an open market.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11

The threat of substitutes is modest. No substitute for valves or hydrants is cited and the metering shift to electronic reading is expected to be slow, so revenue erosion from substitution is not a near-term credit driver.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18

Buyer power is high. Two customers buy 37% of gross sales without long-term contracts, carry competing products and are consolidating, which can intensify pricing pressure and makes revenue and receivables vulnerable to one commercial decision.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 127; calculation M9

Supplier power is moderate. Purchased parts are about 35% of cost of sales, outsourced production reduces control over delivery and cost, and the Israeli plant and imported components carry tariff exposure, so input shocks reach margin before they reach price.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation M12
### PEST

Political and regulatory factors are material through tariffs. U.S. tariffs on imported steel and aluminium rose from 25% to 50%, the Krausz repair products bear most of the cost, and tariffs add about 3% of cost of sales, which dilutes margin even where pricing offsets the dollar cost; the issuer also expects tariffs to raise demand for domestic product, which is an offsetting but unquantified benefit.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 24–26; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 57; calculation M12

Economic factors are material through interest rates, housing and municipal budgets. Rate-sensitive new residential construction is 25% to 30% of sales and municipal spending depends on local taxes and water rates, so a downturn in either reduces volumes. Social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; calculation M10
### SWOT

Strengths in credit terms are low leverage, USD 659.0 million of liquidity, municipal replacement demand from a large installed base, a margin that has risen to 22.79% on reported EBITDA and creditor-aligned policy, which together keep default risk low.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M2; calculation M4; calculation M16

Weaknesses are two customers at 37% of gross sales, price-led and partly non-recurring margins, falling cash conversion and a single 2029 maturity, which together limit how much of the earnings gain is secure.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M9; calculation M5

Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the capacity and cost gains of the foundry programme, demand for domestic product under tariffs and use of cash to repay or refinance the notes ahead of 2029, which would remove the maturity concentration.

Threats that could weaken it are a debt-funded transaction, tariff escalation, a residential slowdown, distributor consolidation or loss, and labour agreements that expire between December 2025 and October 2027, each of which would cut volume or margin.

### Financial profile and credit quality

The business dimensions are favourable but narrow. Scale and market position are Strong, with net sales of USD 1,479.3 million for the latest twelve months and products specified across the largest metropolitan areas, which absorbs shocks; competitive advantage is Strong because installed base and specification let the issuer raise prices with slightly lower volumes; business diversification is Average because 91.89% of sales are in the United States and two customers hold 37%.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation M1; calculation M10; calculation M9

The operating dimensions are Average. Cost and capex flexibility is Average because a significant portion of costs is fixed and the capital expenditure plan rises, margin stability is Average because the 14.60% to 22.79% margin gain is price-led, and free cash flow stability is Average because conversion fell to 43.42% in nine months 2026 and free cash flow was negative USD 2.4 million in FY2022.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 34; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M16; calculation M5; calculation M21

The financial dimensions are Strong. Ability to refinance is Strong because total debt is 1.34x reported EBITDA and the notes were quoted at 96.91% of principal; liquidity is Strong at USD 659.0 million against USD 450.0 million of notes; financial policy and governance are Strong on documented behaviour, with legal capacity not established. The trend is improving on leverage and earnings and softening on cash conversion; the missing datapoints are the fiscal fourth quarter, customer terms and peer data.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

The short-term outlook over the next two years is steady earnings with softer momentum. Fiscal 2026 guidance is net sales of USD 1,470 million to USD 1,480 million and adjusted EBITDA of USD 367 million to USD 372 million, which supports leverage staying low, while the implied fourth quarter and the cut in free cash flow guidance show momentum fading. Tailwinds are water rates up 4.6%, aging infrastructure and a backlog 6.02% above a year earlier; headwinds are a residential slowdown, tariffs, inflation and municipal budget limits.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 56–57; calculation M13; calculation M11; calculation M25; calculation M10

The medium-term outlook over three to five years turns on pricing durability and the 2029 refinancing. Capacity investment in the iron foundries should lower unit cost and support output if demand holds, and the notes and facility mature in 2029, inside the horizon, so how cash is used between now and then decides whether refinancing is a formality or a risk.
### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is a volume shortfall: slower residential construction and municipal deferral coincide with a distributor destocking or repricing, while tariffs and about 4% inflation keep costs rising. The first operational break is the price-cost spread, because fixed foundry and labour costs do not flex, and EBITDA then falls at about 69.51% of lost sales; FY2022 is the supplied precedent, with net sales 15.68% below the latest twelve months and EBITDA 47.81% below.
Basis: 10-K_2024-09-30_mwa-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 94–95; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation M12; calculation M17; calculation M18

Financial transmission runs through working capital. In FY2022 inventories absorbed USD 98.3 million, free cash flow was negative USD 2.4 million and USD 71.5 million was still returned, so cash fell USD 81.0 million. Applied to today's debt, FY2022 EBITDA of USD 176.0 million gives total debt of 2.57x and covers the note coupon 9.78x, and a cash fall of that size leaves liquidity of USD 578.0 million, USD 128.0 million above the notes, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress; this is a precedent-based illustration, not a default case.
Basis: 10-K_2024-09-30_mwa-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 95; calculation M21; calculation M7; calculation M19; calculation M20; calculation M22

Management levers are repurchases, which fell from USD 35.0 million to USD 10.0 million after FY2022, possible deferral of capital expenditures, whose flexibility cannot be measured, and the undrawn facility. The observable triggers are a guidance cut, backlog below USD 320.7 million and free cash flow below 70% of adjusted net income, and the scenario worsens materially only if the unnamed transaction adds debt or the facility is not extended before it ends 91 days ahead of the notes.
Basis: 10-K_2024-09-30_mwa-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation M13; calculation M21
### Overall credit view

Overall, Mueller Water presents a strong business and financial profile supported by low leverage, USD 659.0 million of liquidity and entrenched municipal demand, but credit quality is constrained by price-led margins, two customers at 37% of gross sales and weakening cash conversion. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because municipal replacement anchors demand while earnings and cash conversion rest on pricing. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on whether cash is kept against the notes, which it covers 1.10x, and on extending the facility before 2029-03-16. The primary downside path is a price-led margin reversal with a customer loss and an inventory-driven cash drain, which at FY2022 earnings would leave total debt at 2.57x. Against typical leveraged credit issuers the financial profile looks stronger than the business profile, but that comparison is qualitative because no peer set is supplied. Further analysis would require the fiscal fourth quarter, customer terms, the executed debt documents and peer data. Fundamental credit completed with limitations. Top risk: reversal of price-led margins with two customers at 37% of sales.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M4; calculation M9; calculation M23; calculation M19
